story: At 11:17 on a mild, partly cloudy Thursday in Sumter Oaks, Gary and Donna are both heading out to Magnolia Loop with an eager spring in their step. Hal, meanwhile, is on the street methodically counting the flamingos in Donna's flock and noting the tally against L-02. Back at Rosa's house, she is content, adding a small centerpiece to her dining table and making room for Gary's extra chairs.
events: Gary headed to Magnolia Loop (the street).
Donna headed to Magnolia Loop (the street).
Hal (donna flamingo flock): Count the street-facing flamingos and note the tally against L-02
Rosa (rosa dining table): Add a small centerpiece, check the spacing, and make room for Gary's extra chairs

gary.thought_process: Donna's already told me to grab my sneakers and head to the courts, and I've got water and the good shoes on. I've already said I'm ready, so no need to repeat myself or ask again. The clock is ticking on our two hours (L-05 caps it), and the golf cart wiring is filed and tidy, so nothing's pressing here. Time to get out the door and walk the street toward the courts with Donna.

parameters.content: Heading out with Donna to the pickleball courts for our two-hour lesson

donna.thought_process: We've both said we're heading to the courts, but we're still standing in Gary's house. I already invited him and he agreed, so asking again would be repeating myself. The clock on our two hours is ticking, so the right move is to actually go. The only connection from here is magnolia_loop, which is the way to the courts.

parameters.content: Heading out toward the pickleball courts with Gary so we use our two hours.

hal.thought_process: I'm on Magnolia Loop with no one around, which suits an honest count. My notebook entry says facts only, and I logged my intent last tick. Donna's flamingo flock is right here, so I'll tally the street-facing birds against L-02 before I say a word to anyone. If it's three or fewer, I let it lie and keep the peace for Friday's dinner at Rosa's. If it's over, I've got my number for the committee.

parameters.content: Count the street-facing flamingos and note the tally against L-02

rosa.thought_process: It's Thursday morning and the dinner is Friday. The food is mostly prepped: beans, pork, flan, rice. I've gone through my to-do list several times already and checked the shift schedule, and the table is set for four. Nobody is nearby. The one thing I haven't done is actually put the finishing touches on the dining table, like a centerpiece, and make sure there's room for Gary's chairs. Rather than re-tasting the beans a fourth time, I should do something new and useful with the table so I can stop fussing and get on with my day.

parameters.content: Add a small centerpiece, check the spacing, and make room for Gary's extra chairs

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
